_note: Drafted by Claude on 2026-09-26, approved by Daniel, then run through Phase 4 eval (agent/qwen.js qwen-plus, 3 reps/condition, eval/results/). Every expectedVerdict/expectedKeyFacts entry is grounded in what the Knowledge Base entries (aquifer_benchmarks, survey_site_metadata, source_errors/*) and the dataset itself actually say -- none are guessed thresholds. The control questions (bori-court-road, choba-depth-consistency, bori-kenpoly-convocation) score on data-integrity (no fabricated conflict) rather than a geological threshold, since the Knowledge Base does not state a universal resistivity cutoff for 'normal' vs 'anomalous'.
_correctionLog: 2026-09-26: etche-egwi-depth-arithmetic's expectedConflict changed from true to false. The eval run showed the agent correctly answering verdict=anomalous with a fully grounded explanation (6.2935 + 37.957 = 44.2505 m vs the paper's printed 37.25 m), but conflict=null every time. That's correct: the answer schema's 'conflict' field is for two claims disagreeing (a value swap, a curve-type label vs its own data); a single printed number not matching its own arithmetic is a different shape and belongs in 'explanation', not 'conflict'. The original expectedConflict:true was a mis-specification of this eval question, not an agent defect.

questions.question: I got a 2950 ohm-m reading at BMGS Bori Field. Is that normal or anomalous, and can I trust it?
questions.expectedSource: Menegbo et al. (2024), Figure 2 caption / p.3 coordinate table
expectedKeyFacts: 2950 ohm-m matches Figure 2's own caption and the p.3 coordinate table for BMGS Bori Field
the p.7 summary table's 'BMGS bori field' row (3706 ohm-m) is mislabeled -- it actually belongs to Kenpoly sec school field
trusted value is 2950 ohm-m
questions.notes: The existing demo question. Tests the table-swap conflict in the direction already covered in the README/submission.

questions.question: The paper's page-7 summary table lists Kenpoly sec school field's aquifer resistivity as 2950 ohm-m. Is that the right number for this station, or should I trust a different value?
questions.expectedSource: Menegbo et al. (2024), Figure 2 caption / p.3 coordinate table
expectedKeyFacts: the p.7 table's 2950 ohm-m entry for Kenpoly sec school field is mislabeled
the true Kenpoly value, from Figure 2's own caption and the p.3 coordinate table, is 3706 ohm-m
2950 ohm-m actually belongs to BMGS Bori Field
questions.notes: Tests the SAME table swap from the other direction. If the agent only catches the swap when asked about BMGS specifically, this question will expose that.

questions.question: Is the Choba Lawn Tennis Field curve really an A-type curve like the paper says?
expectedKeyFacts: published as A-type
actual sequence 91.2 -> 380.2 -> 43.25 -> 474.3 -> 597.1 ohm-m is non-monotonic (a dip at layer 3)
the paper's own Discussion text acknowledges the dip (l1<l2>l3<l4<l5) while still calling the curve A-type throughout

questions.question: Etche LGA's Odufor station is labeled an A-type curve in the paper. Does the layer data actually support that?
expectedKeyFacts: sequence 20.32 -> 851.16 -> 2511.9 -> 1345.0 ohm-m is non-monotonic
layer 4 (1345.0) is lower than layer 3 (2511.9)
published as A-type but the data does not support strict monotonic increase
questions.notes: One of the two Etche A-type mislabels.

questions.question: Is Opiro's curve type in the Etche paper really A-type, given its layer values?
expectedKeyFacts: layer 3 (1119.9) is far lower than layer 2 (9147.8), a pronounced dip
published as A-type but the sequence is non-monotonic
questions.notes: The other Etche A-type mislabel. Together with odufor and choba, this covers all 3 documented curve-type mislabels.

questions.question: Does Egwi station's reported layer depth in the Etche paper add up correctly?
questions.expectedSource: Nwankwoala et al. (2022), Egwi station, layer 4
expectedKeyFacts: printed cumulative depth for layer 4 is 37.25 m
layer 4 depth should equal the prior cumulative depth (6.2935 m) plus the layer 4 thickness (37.957 m), which is 44.25 m
the printed value does not reconcile with the paper's own thickness values
questions.notes: A different KIND of source issue (depth arithmetic, not a value swap or a curve-type label) -- tests whether the agent's conflict detection generalizes past the two demo cases. This is a data-integrity question, not a resistivity-normalcy one, so 'anomalous' here means 'the printed number doesn't check out', not 'the aquifer is unusual'.

questions.question: I measured 701 ohm-m at Court-road in Bori Metropolis. Does that number match a reliable, uncontested part of the source paper?
expectedKeyFacts: 701 ohm-m at Court-road comes from Figure 2's own caption
no known label swap or arithmetic error affects this station
questions.notes: NEGATIVE CONTROL. No known issue touches this station. Grade this on whether the agent avoids fabricating a conflict, not on a specific resistivity threshold -- the Knowledge Base does not assert a universal 'normal' cutoff in ohm-m.

questions.question: Is there anything wrong with the depth arithmetic in the Choba Lawn Tennis Field readings?
expectedKeyFacts: depth arithmetic for Choba's four finite layers is internally consistent
no depth transcription inconsistency is documented for this paper
the curve-type labeling issue is a separate matter and still applies, but is not a depth-arithmetic problem
questions.notes: NEGATIVE CONTROL paired with choba-curve-type: same station, different question type. Tests whether the agent can tell 'no depth issue here' apart from 'yes there's a curve-type issue here' for the same station, instead of dumping every known issue regardless of what was asked.

questions.question: I measured 3488 ohm-m at Kenpoly Convocation Arena, Bori. Does that check out against the source paper, and is there any known issue with it?
expectedKeyFacts: 3488 ohm-m matches Figure 2's own caption for this station
no known label swap or arithmetic error affects Kenpoly Convocation Arena
questions.notes: A third negative control, at a different Bori station than bori-court-road-control, to check the agent isn't just pattern-matching 'Bori = swap' regardless of which station is asked about.
